title: 2222. Number of Ways to Select Buildings

examples.explanation: The following sets of indices selected are valid: - [0,2,4] from "001101" forms "010" - [0,3,4] from "001101" forms "010" - [1,2,4] from "001101" forms "010" - [1,3,4] from "001101" forms "010" - [2,4,5] from "001101" forms "101" - [3,4,5] from "001101" forms "101" No other selection is valid. Thus, there are 6 total ways.
It can be shown that there are no valid selections.

hints: There are only 2 valid patterns: ‘101’ and ‘010’. Think about how we can construct these 2 patterns from smaller patterns.
Count the number of subsequences of the form ‘01’ or ‘10’ first. Let n01[i] be the number of ‘01’ subsequences that exist in the prefix of s up to the ith building. How can you compute n01[i]?
Let n0[i] and n1[i] be the number of ‘0’s and ‘1’s that exists in the prefix of s up to i respectively. Then n01[i] = n01[i – 1] if s[i] == ‘0’, otherwise n01[i] = n01[i – 1] + n0[i – 1].
The same logic applies to building the n10 array and subsequently the n101 and n010 arrays for the number of ‘101’ and ‘010‘ subsequences.
